next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Election Calendars

glance_notes.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — 2026 Federal Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Late Voter Registration Available: Montana's regular voter registration closes 30 days before an election, but eligible voters may use late registration after that deadline. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, late registration is available through 5:00 p.m. on the Friday before the election, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Saturday, and through noon on Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voting by Absentee Ballot
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Absentee Voting: Any registered Montana voter may vote by absentee ballot without providing an excuse. Absentee ballots for federal and state elections are mailed to eligible absentee voters 25 days before Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — 2026 Federal Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: Polling Hours Can Vary: Most Montana polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. A polling place with fewer than 400 registered voters who intend to vote there may open later, but must open by noon. Voters should verify their local polling hours before Election Day.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Montana residents may register to vote by submitting a voter registration application to their county election office. To vote, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be at least 18 years old on or before Election Day, have lived in Montana and the county where the person intends to vote for at least 30 days, and meet the state's other voter qualifications. Montana provides regular registration before the 30-day pre-election deadline and late registration after that deadline. During late registration, voters must complete the process through their county election office or another designated location and obtain their ballot in person.
register.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Election FAQs
register.internal_note: The Secretary of State directs voter-registration users to VoteMT.gov and county election administrators. Regular registration closes 30 days before the election, followed by late registration. Montana's late-registration process changed in recent years, so the current 2026 federal election calendar should control over older descriptions of Election Day registration procedures.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Montana's official voter portal to check your voter registration status and absentee status, find your polling place and review other voter-specific election information. If your registration information is incorrect, contact your county election administrator to update it.
check_registration.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voter Portal
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State's 2026 Federal Election Calendar expressly directs voters to the voter portal to check registration and absentee status and find polling-place information.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Montana's regular voter registration closes 30 days before Election Day. Eligible voters who miss regular registration may use late registration by appearing at the county election office or another designated location. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, late registration is available through 5:00 p.m. on Friday, October 30, from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 31, and through noon on Election Day, November 3. A voter using late registration must obtain the ballot in person.
deadlines.glance_value: Late registration through noon on Election Day
deadlines.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — 2026 Federal Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current 2026 Federal Election Calendar directly states that an elector may register or change registration after regular registration closes by appearing at the county election office or designated location before 5:00 p.m. Friday before the election, between 8:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Saturday, or by noon Election Day. The calendar also states that late registrants must obtain their ballot in person. This is more precise than simply saying Montana has unrestricted Election Day registration.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Montana's official voter portal to find your polling place and obtain a map and directions. Polling-place assignments for statewide primary and general elections are based on the voter's registration information. Because locations and hours can vary, voters should verify their polling place before Election Day or contact their county election administrator.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your polling place through the voter portal
polling_place.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voter Portal
polling_place.internal_note: The Secretary of State's 2026 Federal Election Calendar states that the voter portal provides polling-place information, maps and directions. The Secretary also maintains a polling-location and satellite-office page at [https://sosmt.gov/elections/polling-location-satellite-office-locations/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/polling-location-satellite-office-locations/).

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Montana's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Most polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Polling places with fewer than 400 registered voters who intend to vote at the polling place may open later, but must open by noon. Voters must present an accepted form of identification when voting at a polling place. Montana accepts current photo identification as well as certain non-photo documents showing the voter's name and current address.
election_day.glance_value: Most polls 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.; small-location exception
election_day.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — 2026 Federal Election Calendar
election_day.internal_note: The official 2026 Federal Election Calendar directly establishes November 3, the polling-hours rule and current identification guidance. Montana should not be described as having a universal photo-ID requirement because the official 2026 calendar states that a voter without photo ID may present a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, voter-registration confirmation, government check or another government document showing the voter's name and current address.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Most Montana polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. A polling place with fewer than 400 registered voters who intend to vote at that polling place may open later, but must open no later than noon. In qualifying small polling places, a precinct may close once all of its registered voters have voted. Voters should check their polling location and hours before Election Day.
polling_hours.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — 2026 Federal Election Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: Montana Code Annotated 13-1-106 provides the exception. The current 2026 Secretary of State calendar states that polls generally must be open 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m., while a polling place with fewer than 400 registered polling-place voters must open at least from noon to 8:00 p.m. The statute also permits a precinct at such a location to close immediately once all registered electors in that precinct have voted. Avoid the absolute claim that every Montana polling place is open at 7:00 a.m.

early_voting.label: Early / In-Person Absentee Voting
early_voting.content: Montana does not use a separate statewide early-voting system in the same form as many states. Instead, any registered voter may vote absentee without providing an excuse, and voters may obtain and cast an absentee ballot in person through their county election office when ballots are available. Absentee ballots for federal and state elections are mailed to eligible absentee voters 25 days before Election Day. Locations and availability for in-person absentee voting are administered by county election officials.
early_voting.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voting by Absentee Ballot
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State expressly states that any registered voter may vote absentee and that voters can pick up an absentee voting packet at the county election office when ballots are available. This section deliberately uses 'Early / In-Person Absentee Voting' rather than implying Montana has a distinct statutory early-voting period.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Montana voter may vote by absentee ballot without providing an excuse. Absentee ballots for federal and state elections are mailed to eligible voters 25 days before Election Day. A voter may submit an absentee-ballot application by mail or deliver it to the county election office. Applications must be received by noon on the day before the election. If ballots are available, a voter applying in person may pick up the absentee ballot at the same time. Completed absentee ballots must be received by the election office or polling place by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. The voter must sign the affirmation on the return envelope.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; request by noon November 2
absentee_mail.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voting by Absentee Ballot
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes no-excuse absentee voting, the 25-day mailing schedule, noon day-before-election application deadline, in-person pickup and 8:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline. For November 3, 2026, the ordinary application deadline is noon Monday, November 2. A voter changing registration while requesting an absentee ballot during the late-registration period must pick up the ballot from the election office.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Montana voters must present identification when voting at a polling place, but photo identification is not the only option. A voter may present a current photo ID showing the voter's name. If a voter does not have photo identification, the voter may instead present a current utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, voter-registration confirmation notice, government check or another government document showing the voter's name and current address.
voter_id.glance_value: ID required; photo ID is not mandatory
voter_id.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — 2026 Federal Election Calendar
voter_id.internal_note: This section follows the Secretary of State's current 2026 Federal Election Calendar, updated October 2025. It explicitly says all voters must present ID but permits either current photo ID with the voter's name or specified non-photo documents showing name and current address. This avoids incorrectly describing Montana as a strict photo-ID-only state.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Montana provides accessible voting equipment and assistance for voters with disabilities. Every polling place has at least one ExpressVote accessible ballot-marking machine that allows voters to mark a ballot privately and independently. Voters who cannot enter a polling place may request curbside voting. A voter with a physical disability or who cannot read or write may receive assistance from an election judge or another person chosen by the voter, except the voter's employer, an employer's agent or a union agent. Qualified voters with disabilities may also use Montana's Electronic Ballot Request System to request, receive and mark an absentee ballot electronically. The marked ballot must be printed and returned as required by Montana law.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible machines, curbside voting and electronic ballot access
accessible_voting.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly confirms ExpressVote equipment at every polling place, curbside voting, voter-assistance rights and the Electronic Ballot Request System. EBRS is available for state and federal elections beginning 30 days before Election Day through noon the day before Election Day. EBRS allows electronic marking but requires the ballot to be printed and returned by mail or in person. All EBRS ballots must be received by 8:00 p.m. Election Day.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Montana provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for eligible members of the Uniformed Services and Merchant Marine, qualifying spouses and dependents, and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot. Montana's Electronic Absentee System allows eligible military and overseas voters to access and mark their absentee ballot electronically. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Electronic Absentee System is available from September 18 through November 3. Military and overseas voters are also eligible for late registration under Montana law.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and Electronic Absentee System available
military_overseas.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Military & Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current UOCAVA page identifies eligible Uniformed Services, Merchant Marine, spouse/dependent and overseas-citizen categories and provides the FPCA. The page directly establishes September 18-November 3, 2026 availability for Montana's Electronic Absentee System. The 2026 Federal Election Calendar expressly states that absent military and overseas electors are eligible for late registration.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Montana if they meet the state's residence and voter-eligibility requirements. A student who establishes a qualifying Montana residence may use that residence for voter registration. A student who remains registered at another qualifying residence may vote according to the rules for that registration, including absentee voting when applicable. A voter should maintain only one voting residence and should update the registration after establishing a new voting residence.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may register at a qualifying Montana residence
student_voting.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Election FAQs
student_voting.internal_note: Montana voter eligibility is residence-based. No current Secretary of State page located during verification provided a detailed standalone college-student voting guide comparable to some other states. The reader-facing section therefore stays within the general Montana residency and absentee-voting rules and does not claim that attending a Montana college by itself establishes voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Montana voters can use the state's official voter portal and county election resources to review voter-specific election information. Ballot contents depend on the voter's precinct and electoral districts, so voters should use their registered address and county election information when reviewing the contests that will appear on their ballot. General Election ballot information should be checked again after candidate and ballot-issue certification is complete.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check voter portal and county election information
sample_ballot.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Voter Portal
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Secretary of State's voter portal is the official source for voter-specific registration and election information. The 2026 ballot is still developing as of August 30, including statewide ballot-issue and candidate certification processes. Avoid claiming a finalized statewide sample ballot is currently available unless confirmed closer to Election Day.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Montana Secretary of State, Elections and Voter Services, Montana State Capitol, 1301 E. 6th Avenue, Helena, MT 59620. Secretary of State front desk: 406-444-2034. Voter hotline: 1-888-884-VOTE (8683). Elections email: soselections@mt.gov. For voter-specific registration, absentee-ballot, polling-place or local election questions, contact your county election administrator.
contact.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Election & Voter Services
contact.internal_note: The Secretary of State's Elections site verifies the Montana Capitol office and 406-444-2034 front desk. The absentee-voting page directly verifies the 1-888-884-VOTE voter hotline. Current 2026 Secretary of State election materials list [soselections@mt.gov](mailto:soselections@mt.gov). The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Montana Secretary of State Election & Voter Services website and official voter portal for statewide election information. The voter portal provides registration and absentee status and polling-place information. County election administrators maintain local voter registration records, administer absentee voting and late registration, establish polling places and provide voter-specific election assistance.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, voter portal & county election offices
official_resources.source_name: Montana Secretary of State — Election & Voter Services
official_resources.internal_note: Official 2026 election calendars: [https://sosmt.gov/elections/calendars/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/calendars/). Official voter portal: [https://voterportal.mt.gov/](https://voterportal.mt.gov/). Official absentee voting: [https://sosmt.gov/elections/absentee/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/absentee/). Official election FAQs: [https://sosmt.gov/elections/faq/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/faq/). Official accessibility information: [https://sosmt.gov/elections/disabilities/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/disabilities/). Official military and overseas voting: [https://sosmt.gov/elections/military-overseas/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/military-overseas/). Official polling and satellite location information: [https://sosmt.gov/elections/polling-location-satellite-office-locations/](https://sosmt.gov/elections/polling-location-satellite-office-locations/). All source_url values are bare URL strings, and all reader-facing content uses plain text with no Markdown hyperlink syntax.
